record.context_brief: Uniqueness for a coupled elliptic system
record.original_question: Let L and M be elliptic, second-order, selfadjoint, strictly positive Dirichlet operators in a bounded domain D ⊂ R^n with n > 1 and smooth connected boundary S. Assume the coefficients of L and M are real-valued, and let a(x) and b(x) be strictly positive functions that are smooth on the closure of D. If real-valued functions u and v satisfy Lu + a(x)v = 0 and -b(x)u + Mv = 0 in D, together with the boundary conditions u = v = 0 on S, must it follow that u = v = 0 in D? If not, does there exist a counterexample under these stated assumptions?

evidence.quote: Let L and M be elliptic, second order, selfadjoint, strictly positive Dirichlet operators in a bounded domain D in Rn, n > 1, with a smooth connected boundary S... Let Lu + a(x)v = 0 in D, − b(x)u + M v = 0 in D, u = v = 0 on S. (∗) Problem 2: Does (∗) imply u = v = 0 in D? ( ∗∗)
What is of interest is to answer the question as stated, without any additional assumptions, by either proving ( ∗∗) or constructing a counterexample.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, $n>1$, be a bounded domain with smooth connected boundary $S$. Let $L$ and $M$ be second-order, selfadjoint, strictly positive elliptic operators on $D$ with real-valued coefficients, equipped with the Dirichlet boundary condition. Let $a, b \in C^\infty(\overline{D})$ be strictly positive functions on $\overline{D}$. Suppose real-valued functions $u, v$ satisfy
\[
Lu + a(x)\, v = 0 \quad \text{in } D, \qquad -b(x)\, u + Mv = 0 \quad \text{in } D, \qquad u = v = 0 \quad \text{on } S.
\]
Must $u \equiv v \equiv 0$ in $D$? If not, exhibit a counterexample satisfying all the stated hypotheses.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 note by Ramm ("A Uniqueness Result for a Coupled System of Elliptic PDEs", Annals of Mathematics and Physics) establishes the uniqueness conclusion u = v = 0 in the case where a and b are positive constants. The general case with variable positive smooth coefficients a(x), b(x) does not appear to be settled in the literature, so the problem as originally stated is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: A Uniqueness Result for a Coupled System of Elliptic PDEs
status_evidence.snippet: Ramm proves that for the coupled system Lu + av = 0, Mv - bu = 0 with u = v = 0 on the boundary, where L, M are positive selfadjoint elliptic Dirichlet operators and a, b > 0 are constants, the unique solution is u = v = 0.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness is established in the constant-coefficient case a, b > 0.

status_evidence.title: [math/0603631] Three open problems in analysis
status_evidence.snippet: The problem is posed as one of three open problems, asking to either prove u = v = 0 or construct a counterexample under the stated assumptions with general positive smooth a(x), b(x).
status_evidence.claim: The variable-coefficient version of the problem was posed as open.
